questions.q: Resistance of a wire at $0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, 100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $t^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is found to be $10 \Omega, 10.2 \Omega$ and $10.95 \Omega$ respectively. The temperature $t$ in Kelvin scale is _________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{R}=\mathrm{R}_0(1+\alpha \Delta \mathrm{T}) \\ & \frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{R}_0}=\alpha \Delta \mathrm{T}\end{aligned}$
Case-I
$\begin{aligned} & 0{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \rightarrow 100^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ & \frac{10.2-10}{10}=\alpha(100-0)\end{aligned}$  ...(1)
Case-II
$0^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{t}^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\frac{10.95-10}{10}=\alpha(\mathrm{t}-0)$  ...(2)
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{t}}{100}=\frac{0.95}{0.2}=475^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ & \mathrm{t}=475+273=748 \mathrm{~K}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In the given circuit 'a' is an arbitrary constant. The value of m for which the equivalent circuit resistance is minimum, will be x2. The value of x is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Left part of the resistors are connected in parallel, hence R1=am3.

Similarly, for the right part of the resistors we can write, R2=a2m.

Therefore, equivalent resistance will be,

R=am3+a2m

Differentiating both sides w.r.t m to observe critical points, we get dRdm=a3+a-12m2=0

⇒a3=a2m2 ⇒m=32

Thus, x=3.

questions.q: Two identical cells, when connected either in parallel or in series gives same current in an external resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>. The internal resistance of each cell will be ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let r be the internal resistance of each cell.

In above shown figure, first represents the series connection of cells. Second and third figures represents the parallel connection of cells.

Now, in case of series connection, εnet=2ε and rnet=2r. So, current i=2ε5+2r .....(1)

In case of parallel connection, εnet=εr+εrr+r=ε and rnet=r2. So, current i=εr2+5 .....(2)

Equating (1) and (2), we get

2ε5+2r=εr2+5

⇒r+10=5+2r

⇒r=5 Ω.

R=Qi2t=10×10-34×10-6×1=2500 Ω

questions.q: A meter bridge setup is shown in the figure. It is used to determine an unknown resistance R using a given resistor of 15 Ω. The galvanometer G shows null defection when tapping key is at 43 cm mark from end A. If the end correction for end A is 2 cm, then the determined value of R will be Ω.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using the conditions of a balanced wheatstone bridge and adding the end correction.

15R=l+eL+e-l+e⇒1543+2=R102-45⇒R=5745×15

⇒R=19 Ω

questions.q: In the experiment to determine the galvanometer resistance by half-deflection method, the plot of $1 / \theta$ vs the resistance $(\mathrm{R})$ of the resistance box is shown in the figure. The figure of merit of the galvanometer is _____ $\times 10^{-1} \mathrm{~A} /$ division. [The source has emf 2V]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & i=K \theta \\ & \frac{2}{G+R}=K \theta \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\theta}=\frac{(G+R) K}{2}=R\left(\frac{K}{2}\right)+\frac{K G}{2} \\ & \text { Slope }=\frac{K}{2}=\frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow K=0.5=5 \times 10^{-1} A\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A cylindrical wire of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and conductivity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>7</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is subjected to an electric field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mV</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> The expected value of current in the wire will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>π</mi><mo> </mo><mi>mA</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Conductivity σ=5×107 S m-1

Radius r=0.5 mm=5×10-4 m

E=10×10-3 V m-1

J=σE=10×10-3×5×107

⇒J=5×105

⇒iA=5×105

i=5×105×πr2

=5×105×π×5×10-42

=125π×10-3 A

Therefore, i=125 π mA

Hence, x=5

questions.q: As shown in the figure the voltmeter reads 2 V across 5 Ω resistor. The resistance of the voltmeter is _____ Ω
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the resistance of the voltmeter be R Ω. The voltmeter is in parallel with the 5 Ω. So the total resistance in the circuit is 

5R5+R+2 Ω

Applying Ohm's law in the whole circuit, V=IR,

I=3 2+5R5+R A

It is given that the potential difference across 5 Ω is 2 V.

Thus, by Ohm's law,

32+5R5+R×5RR+5=2⇒15+3R10+7R×5R5+R=2⇒15R=20+14R⇒R=20 Ω

questions.q:
The variation of applied potential and current flowing through a given wire is shown in figure. The length of wire is 31.4 cm. The diameter of wire is measured as 2.4 cm. The resistivity of the given wire is measured as x×10-3 Ω cm. The value of x is _____ .

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since, slope of V−I graph represents the resistance, so R=tan45°=1 Ω

Now, resistance of wire is given by R=ρLA 

So, resistivity of the wire is ρ=ARL=πr2RL=π1.22×10-431.4×10-2=1.44×10-3 Ω m=144×10-3Ω cm

questions.q: Twelve wires each having resistance $2 \Omega$ are joined to form a cube. A battery of $6 \mathrm{~V}$ emf is joined across point $a$ and $c$. The voltage difference between $e$ and $f$ is ______V.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: From symmetry, current through e-b & g-d =0 $\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{R}_{\text {eq }}=\frac{3}{4} \times \mathrm{R}=\frac{3}{2} \Omega \\ & \therefore \text { Current through battery }=\frac{6 \times 2}{3}=4 \mathrm{~A} \\ & \mathrm{i}_2=\frac{4}{8} \times 2=1 \mathrm{~A} \\ & \therefore \Delta \mathrm{V} \text { across e-f }=\frac{\mathrm{i}_2}{2} \times \mathrm{R}=\frac{1}{2} \times 2=1 \mathrm{~V} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The figure above shows the current and voltage at different points in circuit.

Applying Kirchhoff's Junction law at A,

x-(y+5)1+x-22+x-02=0    ...1

Applying Kirchhoff's Junction law at B,

y+5-x1+y-01+y-21=0    ...2

Solving equation (1) and (2), we get

x=3 and y=0

Now, at D junction

I1=i1+i2

⇒I1=y-01+x-02

=0-01+3-02

⇒I1=1.5 A.

questions.q: An electric bulb rated as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> is used in a circuit having <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> supply. The resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> that must be put in series with the bulb so that the bulb delivers the same power is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Power, P=V2RB

RB=V2P=100×100200

RB=50 Ω

To produce same power, same voltage (i.e., 100 V) should be across the bulb. 

Hence, R=RB

R=50 Ω

questions.q: Resistance are connected in a meter bridge circuit as shown in the figure. The balancing length l1 is 40 cm. Now an unknown resistance x is connected in series with P and new balancing length is found to be 80 cm measured from the same end. Then the value of x will be _____ Ω.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying balanced condition for meter bridge

Initially, PQ=40 cm60 cm=23       ...1

Finally, P+xQ=80 cm20 cm=41      ...2

Dividing equation 2 by (1,

P+xP=4×32=6

⇒1+xP=6⇒xP=5

∴  x=5P=5×4=20 Ω

questions.q: The current flowing through the $1 \Omega$ resistor is $\frac{n}{10}$ A. The value of $n$ is _________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{y-5}{2}+\frac{y-0}{2}+\frac{y-x+10}{1}=0 \\ & y-5+y+2 y-2 x+20=0 \\ & 4 y-2 x+15=0 \quad \ldots .(\text { (i) } \\ & \frac{x-5}{4}+\frac{x-0}{4}+\frac{x-10-y}{1}=0 \\ & x-5+x+4 x-40-4 y=0 \\ & 6 x-4 y-45=0 \quad . .(i) \\ & \frac{-2 x+4 y+15=0 . .(i i)}{4 x-30=0} \\ & x=\frac{15}{2} \& 4 y-15+15=0 \\ & y=0 \\ & i=\frac{y-x+10}{1} \\ & i=\frac{0-7.5+10}{1} \\ & i=2.5 A=\frac{n}{10} A \\ & n=25\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The length of a given cylindrical wire is increased to double of its original length. The percentage increase in the resistance of the wire will be _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>%</mo></math>
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As volume is constant, so, length doubled and area reduces to half.

Resistance of a wire is given by R=ρlA, where, ρ is resistivity of a material.

Here, R1=ρlA and R2=ρ2lA2=4R

So percentage increase in the resistance will be =4R-RR×100%=300%

questions.q: When a resistance of 5 Ω is shunted with a moving coil galvanometer, it shows a full scale deflection for a current of 250 mA, however when 1050 Ω resistance is connected with it in series, it gives full scale deflection for 25 volt. The resistance of galvanometer is_________Ω.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the maximum current through the galvanometer, when a shunt resistance r1 is connected is given byiGmax=r1r1+RGimax   ...1

When a series resistance r2 is connected, the potential difference across the galvanometer is given by

V=iGmaxRG+r2   ...2

From equations (1) and (2), it can be written that

V=r1r1+RGimaxRG+r2⇒Vr1+VRG=imaxr1RG+imaxr1r2⇒V-imaxr1RG=imaxr1r2-Vr1⇒RG=imaxr1r2-Vr1V-imaxr1   ...3

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required galvanometer resistance.

RG=0.250 A×5 Ω×1050 Ω-25 V×5 Ω25 V-0.250 A×5 Ω=50 Ω

questions.q: An electrical bulb rated <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>220</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></math>, is connected in series with another bulb rated <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>220</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></math>. If the voltage across combination is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>220</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>, the power consumed by the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></math> bulb will be about _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">W</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Electric power is given by P=V2R, here, V is voltage and R is resistance.

Now, for each bulb, R1=V2P=2202100=484 Ω and R2=V2P=220260=484106 Ω

Net current through the series combination is I=220484+484×106 A=0.171 A

Hence, the power consumed by the 100 W bulb is P1=I2R1=14.06 W
